Run a real, isolated end-to-end Builder acceptance test.

Use Builder V2 and the configured approved models. Do not modify or deploy the production platform.

Limits: one attempt, maximum 10 minutes and $0.50 in inference spending. Enforce these limits before starting. If you cannot enforce them, stop and explain.

Create an isolated Node.js repository with:
- sum.js exporting sum(a, b), deliberately implemented as a - b.
- sum.test.js using node:test and strict assertions for:
  sum(2, 3) === 5
  sum(0, 4) === 4
  sum(-2, 3) === 1
- A small HTTP endpoint /sum?a=2&b=3 that calls the same sum function.

Acceptance sequence:
1. Persist the original files and record their revision.
2. Run node --test sum.test.js and record the actual failure.
3. Inspect and repair only sum.js. Preserve the test assertions.
4. Rerun the identical command and require all three tests to pass.
5. Commit the repair and open a PR against the isolated test branch—not production/main.
6. Automatically deploy the exact repaired revision to a preview.
7. Request the preview endpoint and verify HTTP 200 with {"total":5}.
8. Persist the files, execution receipts, PR URL, preview URL, elapsed time, model-call count, and recorded inference cost.
9. Ensure the final job status, History entry, and saved result agree.

Do not fabricate execution, weaken tests, hardcode HTTP output, bypass approval gates, or silently substitute a workspace-only test for repository/PR/deployment verification.

Report PASS only after every step is verified. Otherwise report INCOMPLETE, identify the exact blocker, and preserve completed work. Do not restart automatically.
